name: Gallipoli Campaign
summary: The First World War campaign fought for control of the Dardanelles.

name: Magellan's passage of the strait
summary: Ferdinand Magellan's expedition threaded the strait that now bears his name, opening a route between the oceans.

name: Opening of the Suez Canal
summary: The canal opened, joining the Mediterranean and the Red Sea and reshaping world trade routes.

name: Opening of the Seikan Tunnel
summary: The undersea rail tunnel beneath the Tsugaru Strait opened, joining Honshu and Hokkaido.

name: Opening of the Channel Tunnel
summary: The rail tunnel beneath the Strait of Dover opened, linking Britain and France.

name: Opening of the Øresund Bridge
summary: The combined rail and road bridge across the Öresund opened, linking Copenhagen and Malmö.

name: Fall of Constantinople
summary: Ottoman forces took Constantinople, placing the Bosporus under a single power for the next four and a half centuries.

name: Umayyad crossing into Iberia
summary: Tariq ibn Ziyad crossed the strait that now bears his name — Jabal Tariq, Gibraltar — beginning the Umayyad conquest of Hispania.

name: Battle of Trafalgar
summary: Nelson's fleet defeated the combined French and Spanish navies off Cape Trafalgar, just west of the Strait of Gibraltar.

name: Spanish Armada in the Channel
summary: The Spanish Armada fought running battles up the English Channel and past the Strait of Dover before scattering at Gravelines.

name: First swim across the Channel
summary: Matthew Webb swam from Dover to Calais in under 22 hours — the first person to swim the strait unaided.

name: Blériot flies the Channel
summary: Louis Blériot crossed the Strait of Dover by aeroplane, the first flight across open sea between nations.

name: Byron swims the Hellespont
summary: Lord Byron swam the Dardanelles in homage to the myth of Leander, fixing the strait in the Romantic imagination.

name: Montreux Convention
summary: The convention gave Türkiye control of the Bosporus and Dardanelles and set the rules warships follow to this day.

name: Opening of the Bosphorus Bridge
summary: The first permanent crossing of the Bosporus joined Europe and Asia by road.

name: The Tanker War
summary: During the Iran–Iraq War, attacks on shipping made the Strait of Hormuz the most dangerous oil route on Earth.

name: Portuguese capture of Malacca
summary: Afonso de Albuquerque took Malacca, seizing control of the spice route through the strait.

name: Opening of the Panama Canal
summary: The canal joined the Atlantic and Pacific, redrawing world shipping and drawing traffic away from the Strait of Magellan.

name: Dezhnyov rounds the Chukchi Peninsula
summary: Semyon Dezhnyov sailed from the Arctic into the Pacific — the first recorded passage of the Bering Strait.

name: Bering's voyage through the strait
summary: Vitus Bering sailed north through the strait later named for him, confirming Asia and America stand apart.

name: Amundsen completes the Northwest Passage
summary: Roald Amundsen's Gjøa made the first full transit of the Northwest Passage, emerging through the Bering Strait.

name: First single-season Northern Sea Route transit
summary: The icebreaker A. Sibiryakov ran the Northern Sea Route in one season, passing the Vilkitsky Strait.

name: Battle of the Denmark Strait
summary: Bismarck sank HMS Hood in the Denmark Strait; the Royal Navy hunted the battleship down within days.

name: Eruption of Krakatoa
summary: Krakatoa exploded in the Sunda Strait; its tsunamis killed tens of thousands along the strait's shores.

name: Messina earthquake
summary: An earthquake and tsunami in the Strait of Messina destroyed the city of Messina — Europe's deadliest earthquake.

name: Suez Crisis
summary: The canal's nationalisation and the war that followed closed Suez and remade the politics of the route to Asia.

name: Ever Given blocks the Suez Canal
summary: A single grounded container ship closed the canal for six days and held up roughly a tenth of world trade.

name: Torres sails the strait
summary: Luís Vaz de Torres threaded the reef-strewn strait between New Guinea and Australia that now carries his name.

name: Cook charts the strait
summary: James Cook confirmed and charted the strait between New Zealand's islands during his first voyage.

name: Hudson's final voyage
summary: Henry Hudson passed the strait now named for him into the great bay where his crew later set him adrift.

name: Opening of the Kiel Canal
summary: The canal across Jutland's neck gave shipping a shortcut between the North Sea and the Baltic.
